title: Ambiguity Seduction (The Redesign Spec Fallacy)
pattern: Approving a complete greenfield system rewrite under the assumption that the legacy system can simply be used as a "specification" or that the design is fully understood.
why_bad: Legacy systems are not static specs. They are filled with decades of undocumented edge cases, bug fixes, and critical workarounds. Rewriting them from scratch introduces a massive wave of regressions and misses critical business constraints [102, 104, 106].
detection: Project plans committing to a full rewrite of a highly complex, active legacy system without first writing end-to-end characterization tests to document the actual runtime behavior [406].
counterexample: Valid for isolated, low-complexity modules (e.g. a simple parser utility) with small, well-defined domains.
fix: Avoid full rewrites where possible; instead, iteratively refactor the system in place, extracting highly cohesive subcomponents behind adapters one at a time [122, 165, 215, 393].
source: Kill It with Fire, Chapter 4 [101, 102, 104, 105, 106, 148]; Refactoring [165]; Clean Code [215]
